**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

The ownership/IP allocation in this agreement satisfies the IP rule from our side:

- **We own what we create**: §11.1(a) — title to all know-how, inventions and IP made solely by Ono personnel is owned by Ono. Array's mirror right in §11.1(b) is the permitted "Vendor retains its own IP" position.
- **No assignment of our IP or data to Array**: our Improvements, Data and Ono Know-How remain ours; Array receives only a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free grant-back limited to making/selling the Products and subject to our exclusive rights (§2.6).
- **We own the regulatory assets and brand in our territory**: Ono owns the INDs and Marketing Approvals (§4.4), and Array must assign registered Product Trademarks in the Ono Territory to us (§12.2).
- **Exploitation rights**: exclusive licences under Array Patents/Know-How and Array's interest in the Joint Patents and Joint Know-How, with sublicensing rights (§§2.1–2.2).

Noted in the rationale but not flagged: Joint Inventions are jointly owned with an internal-use/consent restriction (§11.1(c)-(d)), but that restriction is symmetric and expressly disapplied for subject matter licensed to us, so we retain exploitation rights within the deal scope; and our licences are term/territory-limited, which is the core bargain of a territorial in-licence rather than a deliverables engagement.
